lines.text: What if you jumped into a hole straight through the Earth?

phrases.text: What if you jumped into a hole straight through the Earth?

lines.text: First, you'd fall through the crust: about thirty-five kilometers of solid rock.

phrases.text: First, you'd fall through the crust:
about thirty-five kilometers of solid rock.

lines.text: Then the mantle: nearly three thousand kilometers of hot rock.

phrases.text: Then the mantle:

lines.text: Next, the outer core, an ocean of liquid iron.

phrases.text: Next, the outer core,

lines.text: The inner core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.

phrases.text: The inner core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.

lines.text: With no air to slow you, you'd pass the center at about eight kilometers a second.

phrases.text: With no air to slow you,
you'd pass the center at about eight kilometers a second.

lines.text: That's roughly eight times faster than a rifle bullet.

lines.text: Then gravity flips, and starts slowing you down.

lines.text: You coast up the other side and reach the surface, twelve thousand seven hundred kilometers away.

lines.text: Unless someone grabs you, you fall straight back in.

lines.text: The whole trip takes about forty-two minutes.
